title: Famous Eruptions: Vesuvius, Eyjafjallajökull, Kilauea
welcome_lead: Volcanoes have shaped history. Travel back to Pompeii, sit in a grounded aeroplane, then meet Hawaii's lava!

final_note: Brilliant! You can now describe three iconic eruptions.

concepts.def: Italian volcano that destroyed Pompeii in 79 CE.

walkthroughs.body_html: In 79 CE, Vesuvius erupted, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash. The towns were preserved beneath metres of debris, giving us amazing snapshots of Roman life.
In April 2010, this Icelandic volcano sent a huge ash cloud over Europe. Over 100,000 flights were cancelled — ash damages jet engines!
Kilauea is one of the world's most active volcanoes. Its runny lava regularly flows into the sea. In 2018, eruptions destroyed many homes but few people died.
